entities.summary:
The Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) is South Korea’s principal public-service broadcaster, established in its modern form in 1973 and headquartered in Seoul’s Yeouido district. It operates television and radio networks that have been central to national news, drama, and cultural programming.

Under authoritarian and democratic regimes alike, KBS was a battleground over state influence, journalistic autonomy, and the export of Korean popular culture. Its dramas and news bulletins helped standardise a national media sphere before cable and streaming fragmentation.

KBS exemplifies East Asian public broadcasting—caught between government oversight, advertising markets, and global Hallyu soft power.
